newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Richardson has misgivings on Iraqi oil sales deal.
newsitem.headline: Richardson has misgivings on Iraqi oil sales deal.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson said on Thursday Washington needed far more information on implementation of the Iraqi-U.N. oil-for-food deal before it could agree to a rollover of the $2 billion program.

"We are not in a position to say Iraq and the United Nations have implemented the resolution as it was intended," he told reporters about the plan that expires on June 7. "We expected the operation to be far more transparent than it has proven to be in practice."

At issue is an accord that went into effect on December 10 and allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months in order to purchase food, medicine and other goods for its people suffering under U.N. sanctions imposed when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

Richardson, the chief U.S. delegate to the United Nations, said he was concerned about Iraq's distribution methods and U.N. monitoring of the humanitarian goods as well as the implementation of the programme in the Kurdish-dominated north, which receives a separate allocation.

As expected, he said that "you should not expect us to agree on an increase in the volume of oil sales." U.N. officials have said they expected Secretary-General Kofi Annan to recommend $2 billion to the Security Council and not $4 billion as Iraq had wanted.
